findings.message: This host did not provide a verified exact author model for the planning review.

I found no blocking defects. The plan opens with a clear mental model of the pipeline: shipped contract, clean committed snapshot, detached clone, fixed runner, exact reconciliation, then an authenticated external store. It puts the riskiest assumption first, the assertion-identity mapping, and pairs it with a negative control. It also requires a separate run against the actual repository so that fixture-only success cannot count as success.  Coverage is complete: - All 12 blocks and 17 compiled cases are covered, and the counts match the feature file. - The assertion map has 37 cases in 14 blocks, matching the spec. I checked every full_name against the supplied test sources and each one resolves, including the parameter-row expansions in it.each. - Data applicability covers all eleven subjects, and the named owners agree with their sources of truth. - The architecture link resolves to the proposed ARCHITECTURE.md record. - The measurement skip has a concrete reason. - Rollout, rollback, compatibility, crash boundaries, retry, the key-loss case and authority limits are all decided. - The SWM persona's trust, operation and recovery needs each have a design consequence and a confidence limit.  Focused reviewability: pass, with one warning about historical detail in "Current and target truth" (finding 1). The remaining warnings are about clarity and evidence hygiene, not missing decisions.

Focused reviewability passes, but the "Current and target truth" section carries ledger-style detail: review IDs (79aecfba, 82d511e9, 035fe123, 33ce5274, 393dffa4, 4d77aa72), commit SHAs, the 257-pass and 255/257 run counts, and a step-by-step history of the dangling-link, /private/var, basename and stale-Codex-bundle failures. Keep a one-line state per category (implemented, proof available, known defect, pending authority) and the dependency-binding decision. Move the review IDs, SHAs and run counts to the ticket Work Log or a linked evidence file so the decision path stays focused.

Plan-state claims cite fresh scenario review 33ce5274 and Implementation review 393dffa4. Neither appears in the supplied ticket Work Log, whose last entry is "Development". If they are recorded elsewhere, such as quality-review.md, link that record. Otherwise the plan states review facts that the bound ticket context cannot confirm.

The Fixed-assertion row for "Required assertion absent, skipped or failed" says "control child report only", and the Approach says the required result is removed "at the subprocess-output boundary". Both can be read as substituting or editing the runner's report, which R2 forbids ("The observer does not accept a supplied report"). Elsewhere the plan says discrimination comes from committed fixture tests run by the unmodified fixed runner. State explicitly that absent, skipped and failed cases come only from committed fixture test source, never from a substituted or edited report.

The audit exception list includes "a named observer audit-summary output under this ticket", but the plan never says who writes it, where it lives, or what produces it. It also says the observer never writes ticket or historical artifacts. Name the writer and path, or remove the exception, so the R4 "audit-only output" control has a concrete subject that cannot be confused with a loaded execution input.

In the assertion map, case c1dc… ("a different exact model … requested explicit route is absent") reuses the matched-route assertion. That assertion shows exclusion only for codex/gpt-5.6-sol while a codex runtime default is admitted. A test in the same file isolates the different-exact-model condition more directly: the gpt-6-astra-only admission returns []. The plan already marks semantic adequacy as a later-review limit, but a later semantic review should check whether this shared tuple really discriminates both cases.

The PlanEvidenceRecordV1 for the git-clone manual declares license_identifier "none_declared". Git's documentation is distributed under GPL-2.0. This doesn't block anything, since no code or text is reused, but the record should state the actual license or explain why none is declared.
